note: Hand-written search shorthand that no registry ID segment or wiki display name spells out on its own. Every entry here is community shorthand the maintainer is genuinely confident is unambiguous mid-match -- a wrong alias sends a player to the wrong page mid-match, which is worse than a missing one, so this file stays conservative and small on purpose. Add an entry only when the shorthand is widely used, has exactly one sensible target, and is not already produced by pipeline.normalize.aliases.generate_aliases (a whole-phrase or a plain underscore-segment of the entity's own registry ID needs no curated entry). See pipeline/normalize/curated.py for the loader and pipeline/normalize/aliases.py for how a curated alias is weighted against a generated one. One entry was rejected once and is now accepted, and both halves are worth recording. `fort` looked obvious for Fortune and was refused, because this tool is built for draftout matches and in that setting `fort` means the Nether Fortress far more often than it means the enchantment; the refusal noted that structures were not enumerated yet and that the question would need answering the moment Phase 6c landed. It has landed, `minecraft:fortress` is a real entity, and `fort` now points at it rather than at the enchantment it never meant. `dungeon` points at the Monster Spawner rather than at a structure of its own on purpose: a dungeon is a feature, not a `worldgen/structure` member, so it has no page, and the spawner is the block a player is actually looking for when they type it. The three structure nicknames divide into two cases, and the difference is worth keeping straight. `jungle temple` is a name the game itself uses: the structure is `jungle_pyramid`, but its loot table, its biome tag and its structure set are all `jungle_temple`, so the game disagrees with itself and both names are real. `desert temple` and `witch hut` are not that. The game says `desert_pyramid` and `swamp_hut` in every file, and these two are pure community shorthand, which is exactly what this file is for: they are what a player says out loud mid-match, they each have one sensible target, and neither is ambiguous. Do not read the `structure/village/desert/houses/desert_temple_*.nbt` files as evidence for `desert temple` -- those are village houses and have nothing to do with the desert pyramid.
